semanticReview.method: Cotejo de un capítulo académico sobre la estructura informativa japonesa y un artículo académico sobre は／が.
findings: La revisión vigente del coordinador se preservó en docs/r33-local/review-history/MLS-V06-0088/R33A-1791770709148-c6bb24-prior.json (SHA-256 a207172c3d52468bbce8a9a30f36a0227a53619997a8bd16e02872652f675ccd); la copia local antigua, en docs/r33-local/review-history/MLS-V06-0088/worktree-stale-R33W-local-20261012140043-455405.json (SHA-256 e077c37a593b3a24833a1cf40dccb66a1d258b15150ff81a3eaa01143d026126); el artículo anterior, en docs/r33-local/review-history/MLS-V06-0088/article-before-190f85e790887122b2a151695765e5bbea3e03369af8ded3a86822bca3ffe999.json.

Vermeulen (2012) documenta la pregunta dare-ga wain-o nonda no? y la respuesta Taro-ga wain-o nonda, marcando el sujeto de respuesta como foco. La ficha conserva esta atribución y los localizadores de página.
La misma fuente advierte que repetir la oración completa puede resultar poco natural porque la información ya dada suele omitirse; esa limitación se añadió expresamente.

Yoshimoto (1982) distingue la relación sintáctica indicada por ga de las funciones informativas contextuales. No se presenta ga como marcador general de énfasis. APA 7, cobertura por afirmación, hash actual e índice local comprobados; assessEntry aprobó sin errores.
limitations: La regla se restringe al patrón de respuesta de una pregunta parcial con sujeto interrogativo, no a todos los usos de が.

claims.summary: Vermeulen (2012) presents a Japanese constituent question dare-ga wain-o nonda no? and an answer Taro-ga wain-o nonda, marking the answer constituent Taro-ga as focus; the question-answer context identifies the requested subject.

locators.description: Chapter pp. 187–188, section 1.1 “Constituent questions,” example (1): dare-ga wain-o nonda no? / [Taro-ga]F wain-o nonda, English glosses and in-situ description.

claims.summary: The focus reading is identified by the wh-question and its answer context; Yoshimoto (1982) describes ga as marking the syntactic relation between an NP and predicate and distinguishes this from information-structural effects, so ga is not described as a universal standalone emphasis marker.

locators.description: J-STAGE abstract, lines 54–57: ga indicates an NP–predicate relation in syntax; exclusion/new-information interpretation is not peculiar to ga.
Chapter pp. 187–188: distinguishes focus as a question-answer relation from case marking on the answer constituent.

claims.summary: Vermeulen (2012) notes that complete-sentence answers shown in the example are somewhat awkward because given material is preferably unpronounced; the answer constituent alone or a reduced response is more natural.

locators.description: Chapter p. 187, lines 79–92: full sentence answers are “rather awkward”; given items are preferably unpronounced, and constituent responses are described.
